card.title: Dimensions — the homogeneity check that never lies (almost)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Every physical quantity is magnitude plus unit. Seven SI fundamentals (m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd) build all derived quantities. Precision is repeatability of readings; accuracy is closeness to the true value — a precise-but-biased instrument clusters tightly off-target. Significant figures carry the honesty of a measurement: every certain digit plus one doubtful digit.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: dimensions: velocity [LT⁻¹] · force [MLT⁻²] · energy [ML²T⁻²]  ·  homogeneity: every +/− term must share dimensions  ·  errors: mult/div → add % errors; power n → ×n; add/sub → add absolute errors  ·  least count = 1 MSD / VSD

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Homogeneity applies only within one consistent unit system, and only to sums — each added term must match dimensionally. Error-propagation rules assume independent, small, random errors. Significant-figure rules bite only on measured (not counted or defined) numbers.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Systematic error shifts every reading one way (bad calibration); random error scatters both ways (averaging helps only this one). Trailing zeros without a decimal point are ambiguous ('2500' could be 2, 3 or 4 sf). Pure numbers like π, counts and conversion factors carry infinite figures.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Check v² = u² + 2as: [v²] = (LT⁻¹)² = L²T⁻²; [u²] identical; [2as] = L·LT⁻² = L²T⁻². All three terms match → homogeneous, so the equation survives the dimensional filter (NEB 2023, 3 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Homogeneity is necessary but NOT sufficient: v = u + 2at is dimensionally fine yet physically wrong — dimensionless constants (½, 2π) are invisible to the method. It cannot derive sums/differences, trig or exponential relations, and says nothing about numerical correctness.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Derive dimensions from definitions: velocity = displacement/time → L/T = LT⁻¹; acceleration → LT⁻²; force = mass × acceleration → MLT⁻²; work = force × distance → ML²T⁻²; power = work/time → ML²T⁻³. Then a homogeneity check is term-by-term substitution — three lines, full marks.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Memorise the M-L-T ladder: force MLT⁻², energy ML²T⁻², power ML²T⁻³, pressure ML⁻¹T⁻², charge IT, voltage ML²T⁻³I⁻¹. For error questions: multiplication → add percentage errors, power → multiply by the exponent. 'Check correctness' always means homogeneity first.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): state the principle of homogeneity of dimensions and check v² = u² + 2as. NEB 2024 (2): accuracy vs precision with an example. NEB 2023 (2): four fundamental quantities with SI units + define the kilogram.
